findings.text: Several new `obj` contexts give the wrong place. On this line, `before["runtime"]` is labeled `.runtime.files`. On line 96, `before[field]` is labeled `.{field}.files`, and on line 99, `before["source"]` is labeled `.source.files`. On line 107, the `before["helpers"]` object and its `files` map in `linux/identity-before.json` are both labeled "helper entry {name}". So a shape error in the parent object points to the wrong field. Fix: give each `obj` call the path of the value it narrows, for example `linux/identity-before.json.runtime` for the outer call and `linux/identity-before.json.runtime.files` for the `files` map.

These contexts do not say which artifact had the wrong shape. Here, `report[side]` and `original[side]` both get the label `f"{side} evidence"`. On line 101, the source-manifest entry and the identity-before entry both get `f"source entry {name}"`. On line 148, the label is "linux/identity-before.json source or archive" and does not name one field. Fix: put the artifact name and the field in each label, for example `f"linux/report.json.{side}"` and `f"{HISTORICAL_RECORD}.{side}"`, and use `linux/identity-before.json.source` or `linux/identity-before.json.archive` on line 148.

The shape diagnostic of `obj` now names an artifact and a field, but no committed test checks it. `check_mutations.py` does not exercise malformed shapes. The malformed-shape check that the status file describes was a manual run, so it does not stop a regression. Fix: add a malformed-shape case to `check_mutations.py` that asserts that the error message contains the expected artifact and field path.
